Console models

OpenCode Console provides a list of models tested and verified by the OpenCode team. Sign in, add credits, and get an API key to use them with OpenCode or another coding agent.

Console works like any other provider in OpenCode. It’s completely optional, and you can use any other provider instead. For a subscription with included usage, see OpenCode Go.

  1. Sign in to the console, add your billing details and credits, and copy your API key.

  2. Run /connect in the TUI, choose the OpenCode pay-as-you-go provider, and paste your API key.

    /connect

  3. Run /models to see the available models and select one.

    /models

You are charged per request and can add credits to your account.

You can also access the models directly through the following API endpoints. Free-tier chat models require OpenCode; use paid models or Go from other clients.

Each model is listed with its native API, but every text model also works through the other APIs, which Console translates. See Base URLs for the full set.

These AI SDK packages are for applications calling the endpoints directly. To select a model in OpenCode, use the format opencode/<model-id>:

opencode.jsonc
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "model": "opencode/gpt-6.1-sol",
}

Fetch the full list of available models and their metadata from the models endpoint:

Terminal
curl https://opencode.ai/inference/v1/models

See the model list API for every field in the response, and for the Console list that also includes the providers your workspace connected.

Jev is a System One model from TypeSafe AI for fast, structured decisions. Instead of generating text, it evaluates a state against typed questions and returns values and probabilities that your code can use directly. It supports yes/no (noul), multiple-choice (choice), and rubric-based (score) questions.

Use your OpenCode Console API key with the https://opencode.ai/inference/systemone/v1/systemone endpoint. This example checks whether a support request is urgent:

Terminal
curl https://opencode.ai/inference/systemone/v1/systemone \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPENCODE_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "jev-1.13",
    "state": "My payments have failed for three days and I am losing sales. Please help now.",
    "questions": {
      "is_urgent": {
        "type": "noul",
        "instructions": "Does this request require urgent attention?"
      }
    }
  }'

You can ask multiple questions in one request. Jev evaluates them in parallel and returns each answer under the matching question ID:

Terminal
curl https://opencode.ai/inference/systemone/v1/systemone \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPENCODE_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "jev-1.13",
    "state": "My order arrived late and the item is damaged. I want a refund.",
    "questions": {
      "department": {
        "type": "choice",
        "instructions": "Which team should handle this request?",
        "criteria": {
          "returns": "Refunds, exchanges, or damaged items",
          "shipping": "Delivery delays or lost packages",
          "billing": "Charges, invoices, or payment problems"
        }
      },
      "frustration": {
        "type": "score",
        "instructions": "How frustrated is the customer?",
        "criteria": ["Calm", "Frustrated", "Very angry"]
      }
    }
  }'

Use jev-1.13-free instead of jev-1.13 to use the limited-time free model. See the TypeSafe AI documentation for details about question types and response fields.

gpt-6-luna-decision and gemini-decision-1 take the same System One request as Jev, on the same endpoint. Pass images, audio, video, and PDFs in state as chat-style parts (image_url, input_audio, video_url, file). GPT 6 Luna Decision accepts text and images; Gemini Decision 1 also accepts audio, video, and PDFs.

Terminal
curl https://opencode.ai/inference/systemone/v1/systemone \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPENCODE_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "gemini-decision-1",
    "state": "I was charged twice for my order.",
    "questions": {
      "refund": {
        "type": "noul",
        "instructions": "Is this a refund request?"
      }
    }
  }'

gpt-image-2.5-sunburst, gemini-nano-banana-2.1, and grok-imagine-image-2.0 generate and edit images. They aren’t chat models, so they never appear in /models or the models endpoint, and opencode/<model-id> doesn’t select them. Call them on their native API with a Console key, or let OpenCode’s experimental_image_generate tool use an image model by setting experimental.image_generate.model, for example opencode/gpt-image-2.5-sunburst.

Terminal
curl https://opencode.ai/inference/openai/v1/images/generations \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPENCODE_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "gpt-image-2.5-sunburst",
    "prompt": "A mountain at sunrise",
    "size": "1024x1024"
  }'

Google takes its native contents and generationConfig, and xAI its native options such as resolution and quality. OpenAI Images and xAI Images also accept edits at /images/edits.

All our models are hosted in the US and EU. Our providers follow a zero-retention policy and do not use your data for model training, with the following exceptions:

  • Big Pickle: During its free period, collected data may be used to improve the model.
  • Iceman Free: During its free period, collected data is retained and used to improve the model.
  • Inkling 2 Small Free: During its free period, collected data is retained and may be used to monitor the model’s real-world performance and for model training. See Thinking Machines’ Terms of Service and Privacy Notice.
  • Flint 40B Free: During its free period, collected data may be used to improve the model. Data is retained for 30 days.
  • Nemotron 3.5 Lightning Free (NVIDIA free endpoints): Trial use only — do not submit personal or confidential data. Your use is logged for security purposes and to improve NVIDIA products and services. The logged session data for improvement purposes is not linked to your identity or any persistent identifier. For more information about our data processing practices, see our Privacy Policy. By interacting with this endpoint, you consent to our collection, recording, and use of such information and the NVIDIA API Trial Terms of Service.
  • Nemotron 3.5 Super VL Free (NVIDIA free endpoints): Trial use only — do not submit personal or confidential data. Your use is logged for security purposes and to improve NVIDIA products and services. The logged session data for improvement purposes is not linked to your identity or any persistent identifier. For more information about our data processing practices, see our Privacy Policy. By interacting with this endpoint, you consent to our collection, recording, and use of such information and the NVIDIA API Trial Terms of Service.
  • OpenAI APIs: Requests are retained for 30 days in accordance with OpenAI’s Data Policies.
  • Anthropic APIs: Requests are retained for 30 days in accordance with Anthropic’s Data Policies.
  • Mistral APIs: Prompts and other inputs are not used for training. Data is retained in accordance with Mistral’s Data Retention Policy.
  • Google APIs: Requests are retained for up to 55 days for abuse monitoring in accordance with Google’s Gemini API Terms.
  • xAI APIs: Requests are retained for 30 days in accordance with xAI’s Privacy Policy.
  • Beam Free: Prompts and other inputs are not used for training. Data is retained for 30 days for safety reasons.
  • LongCat 2.5 Free: Hosted in China. Prompts and other inputs are not used for training or retained.

For subscription models, see Go privacy.

Share Console models with your team from a workspace. Owners and admins can invite members, choose which models are enabled from the Models tab, set budgets, and connect their own providers.

There are many models available, but only a few work well as coding agents. Providers also vary in configuration, performance, and quality, so a model accessed through a gateway such as OpenRouter may perform differently.

Tip
We tested a select group of models and providers that work well with OpenCode.

To build this catalog, we:

  1. Tested a select group of models and talked to their teams about how to best run them.
  2. Worked with providers to make sure the models were served correctly.
  3. Benchmarked each model/provider combination to produce a list we feel good recommending.

Console is an AI gateway that gives you access to these models.

We built Console to:

  1. Benchmark the best models and providers for coding agents.
  2. Provide the highest quality options without downgrading performance or routing to cheaper providers.
  3. Pass along price drops by selling at cost, with markup only to cover processing fees.
  4. Have no lock-in: use Console with any coding agent, or use another provider with OpenCode.
